elements.title: Outreach message
elements.what: A message to an offline maker with the open demand for what they make, plus links to sign up and to a 5-minute cost check.
elements.why: Makers who aren’t on Meesho never see its demand; we take the demand to them first.

elements.title: Demand teaser at sign-up
elements.what: Arriving from the outreach link, the sign-up side panel shows the maker’s own product demand instead of generic stats.
elements.why: The first screen answers the maker’s real question: is there demand for what I make?

elements.title: 5-minute cost check
elements.what: Product type + making cost → every fee, break-even, take-home at any price, and whether a qualifying price exists.
elements.why: A maker decides on what they keep, not on the selling price, so we show take-home before they sign up.

elements.title: Seller-type question, moved to step 1
elements.what: Meesho’s own business-type question, asked right after the GST fetch instead of in the last step.
elements.why: Today it’s self-declared and never used; we use it to tell makers from resellers.

elements.title: GST and Udyam checks
elements.what: GST nature of business and Udyam activity are matched to the seller type → eligible, pending or not eligible.
elements.why: Factory Launch is for real manufacturers, so records decide, not a self-declared answer. Resellers keep selling as today.

elements.title: Pack Point or self-ship
elements.what: Once the pickup address saves: ship through the Cluster Pack Point (one bulk lot a week) or self-ship as today.
elements.why: Many offline makers can’t pack and ship single orders; the Pack Point does it for the whole cluster.

elements.title: Create from photos
elements.what: A third way to upload, next to Single and Bulk: start a listing from a few phone photos.
elements.why: Listing is where new makers stall; photos are something every maker already has.

elements.title: Product screen, filled by the bot
elements.what: Category, cleaned-up images, title and attributes are pre-filled from the photos and marked as filled; the maker adds only what a photo can’t tell.
elements.why: Most of today’s mandatory fields are filled for the maker, and every field stays editable.

elements.title: Demand and first lot
elements.what: Quantity screen: open demand for the product type, the listing’s likely share, and a suggested first lot the maker can lower.
elements.why: Makers make to demand: the first lot is sized from expected sales, not guessed.

elements.title: Take-home and Qualifies chip
elements.what: Price screen: making cost and margin in → every fee, break-even, list price, take-home and a Qualifies / Doesn’t qualify chip.
elements.why: Today the maker types a price with no fees or take-home shown. Now they see what they keep, while the launch price cap stays hidden.

elements.title: Go-live checklist
elements.what: Images, details, price in band and lot are ticked before Go live, with fees locked at dispatch.
elements.why: Today Submit Catalog sends the listing straight to QC; the checklist catches problems first, and the payout matches the quote.

elements.title: EN / हिंदी toggle
elements.what: The listing bot’s screens switch between English and Hindi.
elements.why: The panel is English-only today; many makers are more at home in Hindi.

elements.title: Factory Launch tab
elements.what: A new event type in Promotions, next to Sale Events, Deals and Flash Events.
elements.why: Gives makers a launch route that asks for stock and a fair price, not a discount.

elements.title: Order book
elements.what: Slots per product type, expected orders per listing, suggested first lot, how much is committed so far, and the key dates.
elements.why: Makers commit stock against published demand. The price cap is checked at commit, never printed.

elements.title: Eligibility by rule
elements.what: Eligible makers just see Commit; a maker who fails a check sees “not eligible” and why.
elements.why: Entry is decided by records and price, not by who opts in.

elements.title: Commit stock
elements.what: Pick the SKU and the units (lot suggested, any number), the price is re-checked, then Commit. No discount field.
elements.why: A launch slot is earned with stock and a qualifying price.

elements.title: Next Factory Launch card on Home
elements.what: Home step 3 “Get your first order” shows the next launch with slots left, then the launch’s progress.
elements.why: Step 3 offers no help today; this gives the first order a date.

elements.title: Live launch view
elements.what: During the launch: orders each day against the expected range, and units sold of the committed lot.
elements.why: The maker sees the promised demand arrive, day by day.

elements.title: Listing-level quality score
elements.what: Quality shows a score for this listing, built from its own launch orders and returns.
elements.why: New listings show “No score available” today; launch orders build the listing’s own track record.

elements.title: Your listing’s own numbers
elements.what: The Business Dashboard’s existing tiles and product table, filled with the launched listing’s week.
elements.why: The growth loop reads numbers Meesho already shows each seller; nothing new is collected.

elements.title: Restock card
elements.what: On Inventory → Low Stock: run-rate, days of cover, reorder point, next batch, and dates to start and land it.
elements.why: Low Stock lists SKUs with no guidance today; the maker gets a dated production plan.

elements.title: SKU Health Coach
elements.what: One SKU, one cause, one fix a week, at the top of the Business Dashboard and on Home.
elements.why: The dashboard shows numbers only; the coach says what to change.

elements.title: Per-SKU funnel
elements.what: The coached SKU’s own views, clicks, orders and conversion. The trigger that fired stays internal.
elements.why: The fix is tied to that listing’s numbers, not to seller-wide totals.

elements.title: Make-to-demand verdict
elements.what: A chip on each SKU in Inventory: Make more, Keep, Fix, Stop or Switch, with a one-line reason.
elements.why: Tells the maker what to produce next, not just what’s in stock.

elements.title: What to make instead
elements.what: For a SKU marked Stop: open-demand products on the same production line.
elements.why: Factory time moves to products buyers are already asking for.

elements.title: Price position tab
elements.what: A new Manage Pricing tab: for each SKU, whether the price qualifies and which third of similar listings it sits in.
elements.why: Makers see where they stand without seeing the cut-off, so it can’t be gamed.

elements.title: Price-hold breach
elements.what: If an edited price no longer qualifies: “slot removed” on Manage Pricing and the launch listing, with no number shown.
elements.why: The launch price has to hold after the launch, or buyers lose the saving.

elements.title: Cluster Pack Point program
elements.what: A second program card on Warehouse: one lot a week, the partner packs, ships and takes returns; self-ship stays available.
elements.why: Meesho Warehouse serves top sellers in three cities; makers in clusters need a shared node.

elements.title: Pack Point fee card
elements.what: The fee per delivered order and how it’s built, the maker’s own cost stack with it, and which clusters are live.
elements.why: The fee only works with enough makers per node, so the card shows the density gate.

elements.title: Lot inbound
elements.what: The first lot sized from demand, received, counted, and every unit weighed.
elements.why: Weights at inbound make every later claim provable.
